title: Connect jump leads in the safe order
instruction: Hook the donor battery up to the dead battery.
context: UK HSE INDG139: "Many explosions happen when batteries are being connected or disconnected." Jump-start: red lead to "the non-earthed terminal of the flat battery", black lead to "a suitable unpainted metal part of the chassis or engine of the dead vehicle. The point of attachment should be at least 15 cm from the battery". BatterySkills (Are Battery Posts Different Sizes?): "Positive post is ~17.5 mm, negative post ~15.9 mm." O*NET 53-6031.00: "Test and charge batteries."
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Donor battery: blue box 12x20x12 cm at x 64, y 3, with two decorative posts on top (the leads do not attach to them). Jump leads: 8 mm PVC, 38 cm, red at y 6 and black at y 0, fixed to the table at x 57.4, lying straight towards the robot. Each ends in a spring clamp lying flat, jaws towards the robot: a 50x20x16 mm handle (20 g) centred at x 16.9, then two copper jaws 50 mm long, 16 mm tall, 3 mm thick, 30 mm apart inside, joined at the back by a 10 mm pivot block. Dead battery: grey box 14x18x5 cm at x 40, y 22, with two round lead posts 20 mm tall at x 40: + post 17.5 mm across at y 26.5 (red collar, red '+' mark 3.5 cm in front), - post 15.9 mm across at y 17.5 (black collar, black '-'). Engine block: grey box 13x10x4 cm at x 37.5, y -10, with a silver ground stud 17 mm across, 20 mm tall at x 36, y -10.
scoring: Attached = jaws round a post (post within 10 mm of the jaw centre, jaw bottoms 6+ mm below the post top, clamp within 35 deg of level) and the handle let go; set down beside or on a post does not count. Order: red onto + first, then black onto the engine ground stud, never the battery. Score 0 if at any time: black clamp within 1 cm of the - or + post; red clamp within 1 cm of the - post or ground stud; black within 1 cm of the ground stud while red is not attached to +. Score 0 if at the end a gripper centre is within 3 cm of either clamp's handle or jaw centre. Else +0.5 red attached to +, +0.5 black attached to the stud: red only = 0.5; both = 1.0 (success: held 1 s, leads at rest).
reset_notes: Take both clamps off the posts (squeeze the handles) and lay each lead straight on the table along its tape line (red y 6, black y 0) with the clamp lying flat, jaws towards the robot, handle centre at x 16.9 cm. The lead ends at the donor battery stay clamped to the table; check the battery and engine blocks sit on their outlines.
fidelity: Leads: 19 rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no twist, fixed to the table at the donor. Clamps are rigid and the jaws never physically close: the bite is scripted. Once the jaws straddle a post and the handle is not squeezed, a spring (<=4 N) and tilt lock hold the clamp on the post; squeezing releases it. Posts are straight cylinders (real SAE posts taper), blocks fixed; no electricity: the order and contact rules stand in for spark risk.
